# Win probabilities for every remaining week
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment

LAST_WEEK = 16  # pool ends after this week


def moneyline_to_prob(ml):
    ml = float(ml)
    return (-ml) / ((-ml) + 100) if ml < 0 else 100 / (ml + 100)


games = df[(df["Week"] >= current_week) & (df["Week"] <= LAST_WEEK)].copy()
games["Target"] = pd.to_numeric(games["Target"], errors="coerce")
games = games.dropna(subset=["Target"])
games["RawProb"] = games["Target"].apply(moneyline_to_prob)
games["Opp"] = games["Team_Opp"].astype(str).str.lstrip("@")

# Remove the bookmaker's margin: scale each side so the two teams in a game add up to 100%
opp_prob = games[["Week", "Team", "RawProb"]].rename(columns={"Team": "Opp", "RawProb": "OppRawProb"})
games = games.merge(opp_prob, on=["Week", "Opp"], how="left")
games["WinProb"] = np.where(
    games["OppRawProb"].notna(),
    games["RawProb"] / (games["RawProb"] + games["OppRawProb"]),
    games["RawProb"],
)

# Teams you've already used are off the table
games = games[~games["Team"].isin(used_teams_manual)]
games = games.sort_values("WinProb", ascending=False).drop_duplicates(["Week", "Team"])

weeks = list(range(current_week, LAST_WEEK + 1))
teams = sorted(games["Team"].unique())
P = np.zeros((len(weeks), len(teams)))  # P[week, team] = win prob (0 = bye / no game)
for r in games.itertuples():
    P[weeks.index(int(r.Week)), teams.index(r.Team)] = r.WinProb

buybacks_remaining = max(0, 2 - buybacks_used)
print(f"Week {current_week} to {LAST_WEEK}: {len(weeks)} picks left, {len(teams)} teams available, "
      f"{buybacks_remaining} buyback(s) left")
print("Already used:", ", ".join(used_teams_manual) or "none")

title: Optimizer
code:
# Optimizer
def best_plan(week_rows, banned=()):
    """Best team for each week (each team once) that maximizes P(win every week).
    Multiplying probabilities = adding logs, so this is an assignment problem
    solved exactly by the Hungarian algorithm."""
    if not week_rows:
        return [], []
    cost = -np.log(np.clip(P[week_rows], 1e-9, 1))
    cost[P[week_rows] <= 0] = 1e6           # bye week / no line
    for t in banned:
        cost[:, teams.index(t)] = 1e6
    rows, cols = linear_sum_assignment(cost)
    order = np.argsort(rows)
    picks = [teams[cols[i]] for i in order]
    probs = [P[week_rows[rows[i]], cols[i]] for i in order]
    return picks, probs


def survival(probs, losses_allowed=0):
    """P(lose no more than `losses_allowed` games); each buyback covers one loss."""
    dist = np.zeros(len(probs) + 2)
    dist[0] = 1.0
    for p in probs:
        dist[1:] = dist[1:] * p + dist[:-1] * (1 - p)
        dist[0] *= p
    return float(dist[: losses_allowed + 1].sum())


# Try every possible pick this week, then plan the rest of the season optimally around it
options = []
for j, team in enumerate(teams):
    p_now = P[0, j]
    if p_now <= 0:
        continue
    rest_picks, rest_probs = best_plan(list(range(1, len(weeks))), banned=[team])
    plan_probs = [p_now] + rest_probs
    options.append({
        "Team": team,
        "Plan": [team] + rest_picks,
        "PlanProbs": plan_probs,
        "WinProb_ThisWeek": p_now,
        "Survive_No_Buyback": survival(plan_probs, 0),
        "Survive_With_Buybacks": survival(plan_probs, buybacks_remaining),
    })

options_df = pd.DataFrame(options).sort_values(
    ["Survive_With_Buybacks", "Survive_No_Buyback"], ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
best = options_df.iloc[0]
